geo.label: Fed on hold; 2024 cuts priced early
parts: Macro Stance

The US goes into the last days of November priced for a finished Fed. Reuters reports the dollar weakening as the rate-cut view weighs [[n0098]], and Business Insider says it is on pace for its worst month of 2023 on bets that the Fed is done raising rates [[n1789]]. Risk assets have taken the hint: the S&P 500 closed at 4,550.43, up 10.52% over 20 sessions, and VIX sits at 12.69 after a 40.34% 20-session collapse (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). We hold a Mixed stance rather than a Bullish one because the rally is running ahead of the data. The four-week winning streak cooled in Monday's session [[n0155]], and existing-home sales hit a 13-year low in October as the housing freeze deepened [[n1710]].
Rates & Curve

The curve has done the Fed's easing for it. The 2Y closed at 4.84% and the 10Y at 4.39%, leaving 10Y−2Y at −45 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 15 bps and the 10Y 45 bps, a bull flattening that deepened the inversion, while the 30Y dropped 50 bps and the 3M only 10 bps because the front end stays tied to a policy rate the latest Fed minutes say must stay high [[n0294]]. Momentum is fading: over five observations the declines shrank to 4 bps at the 2Y and 5 bps at the 10Y. Bank of America now argues cuts are coming next year [[n1786]], but $7.6 trillion of US government debt maturing within a year is a supply wall that can rebuild term premium [[n0135]].
New / Most Important

The holiday weekend delivered volume bought at a discount. CNBC reports Black Friday shoppers spent a record $9.8 billion in US online sales, up 7.5% from last year [[n0132]], yet Reuters described a 'lot quieter' Black Friday that brought out discount hunters [[n1579]]. That split fits October's data: retail sales slipped as consumers pulled back after summer splurges [[n1687]], and producer prices slid 0.5%, the biggest drop since 2020 [[n1688]]. Disinflation with resilient nominal spending is exactly the soft-landing mix the market is paying for; the bill arrives in fourth-quarter retail gross margins, where markdowns absorb the volume.
Playbook ✓

Stay long duration in the belly and add quality equities on pullbacks, but do not chase beta with VIX at 12.69 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Trigger to add: a 10Y close below the 4.39% prior close while unemployment holds near October's 3.9% [[n1664]], which would confirm cooling without a break. What changes the call: a front-end backup that lifts the 2Y back toward the 4.99% it yielded 20 observations ago, which would mean cuts were over-discounted (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). Hedge equity length with index volatility while it is cheap; Goldman's finding that hedge-fund bets on US stocks are the most crowded ever makes an unwind the asymmetric risk [[n0303]].

geo.label: ECB on hold; German fiscal brake bites
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is the weak link in the developed-market soft landing. Reuters reports Germany's economy shrank slightly in the third quarter [[n0995]], Berlin froze government spending as its budget crisis deepened [[n0983]], and DW describes a country grappling with its constitutional debt brake [[n1007]]. Equities have rallied anyway on global duration: the Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 4,354.41, up 8.09% over 20 sessions, and the DAX at 15,966.37 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). We are Bearish because that rally rests on lower yields, not on earnings.
Activity & Inflation

Output is contracting while the ECB refuses to declare victory. Euro-area GDP dipped 0.1% in Q3 [[n0956]], yet Lagarde warned against a premature inflation celebration [[n0979]] and ECB policymaker De Cos called rate-cut talk premature [[n0975]]. The transmission channel to watch is credit: the ECB warns eurozone banks are starting to show stress as loan defaults rise [[n0986]]. Frozen German fiscal support plus unchanged policy rates is a stagnation mix, negative for cyclicals and supportive of core bonds.
New / Most Important

The most important new datapoint is corporate. Reuters reports Volkswagen will reduce headcount at a core VW brand it calls 'no longer competitive' [[n0747]], Germany's cost problem compressed into one sentence. The steel sector warns that the German budget hole puts industry at risk [[n0510]]. Beneath the index, autos lag: the STOXX autos tracker fell 1.04% over five sessions while the DAX gained 0.41% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Playbook ✓

Underweight European cyclicals and autos against US quality, and own core European duration as the hedge for an ECB that eventually capitulates. Trigger to cover: a German budget fix that unfreezes investment, confirmed by the Euro Stoxx 50 holding above 4,354.41 while autos stop underperforming. What changes the call: a services-inflation rebound that pushes Bund yields higher despite contraction, which would hurt the duration leg and the equity rally at the same time.

geo.label: PBOC easing bias; targeted property and market support
parts: Macro Stance

China is in a policy-supported stall: Beijing is using administrative tools to stabilise markets and developers, but profits and prices still show demand too weak to sustain itself. Reuters reports industrial profits growth slowed in October, keeping stimulus calls alive [[n0224]], while the People's Bank governor pledged to support growth and urged reforms [[n0230]]. Prices reflect the stalemate: the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,031.70, down 1.19% over five sessions and up only 0.34% over 20, and the Hang Seng at 17,525.06 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Mixed is the right stance: policy floors exist, a demand catalyst does not yet.
PMIs & Activity

The October data set the tone. Caixin's PMI confirmed a manufacturing slump [[n0158]], and exports fell for a sixth straight month even as imports rose [[n0162]]. Consumer prices slipped back into decline as the recovery wobbled [[n0161]], and Bloomberg reports the labour market is weaker than official data show [[n0194]]. Profits were still up in October [[n0231]], but for capex intentions the deceleration matters more than the level. Economist Yu Yongding is flagging stagflation risks [[n0188]], an unusual framing with consumer prices falling that reflects weak output alongside cost pressure on households. The next official PMI is the test of whether October's slump was a one-off.
Credit Impulse

Credit is being steered rather than broadly expanded. Reuters reports China's high-tech manufacturing loans are raising fears of a wave of cheap exports [[n0164]]: lending is flowing to capacity, not to households. The shadow side is cracking, with The Guardian reporting a Chinese shadow bank admitting a £30bn shortfall after 'management ran wild' [[n0209]], a loss that ultimately lands on wealthy savers and on developer funding. The impulse that matters for metals and commodity currencies is household and developer credit, and copper's two-month peak on China demand hopes [[n0175]] has already faded: the front-month contract closed at 3.76 USD/lb, down 1.31% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Property

Property remains the binding constraint, but the response is escalating. The Business Times reports Beijing weighing unprecedented builder support with first-ever unsecured loans [[n0208]], and Shenzhen cut down payments on second homes as cities try to revive demand [[n0214]]. The price data say those steps are needed: more Chinese cities recorded falling home prices in October [[n0170]]. The Financial Times' reporting on the human cost of the crisis [[n0245]] explains why household confidence repairs slowly, even as an SCMP opinion piece argues China's property crisis will not produce Japan-style lost decades [[n0243]]. Unsecured lending would be a regime shift, credit to developers on trust rather than collateral, and the first concrete allocation is the trigger for Hong Kong property and metals.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The external climate is softening at the margin. China approved the Broadcom-VMware merger with conditions, which SCMP reads as a sign of thaw with the US [[n0465]], and Beijing offered visa-free entry to citizens of France, Germany and Italy [[n0558]]. Reuters reports finance veteran Zhu will be named forex chief [[n0196]], while the yuan traded near a four-month high on firmer fixings and steadier China-US ties [[n0187]]. Friction has moved to technology: Nvidia shares closed down on a report it delayed a China AI chip designed to comply with US export rules [[n0218]], and India's chemical industry is seeking higher duties on Chinese imports [[n0229]]. A firmer yuan loosens the external constraint on PBOC easing.
Markets & Flows

The equity market is now partly administered. Reuters reports the Beijing bourse told 'major shareholders' to refrain from selling [[n0236]], and the CSI 300 biannual review leaned towards tech firms [[n0233]]. Offshore wrappers still slipped in the latest session: ASHR fell 1.07%, FXI 1.29% and KWEB 1.89%, although KWEB kept a 5.78% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Leadership is idiosyncratic. Baidu's US line is up 14.71% over five sessions after its third-quarter call [[n0391]], while Alibaba's Hong Kong shares are down 7.03% over 20 sessions after Jack Ma reversed a plan to sell shares as the stock dropped [[n0190]]. Tencent, at 322.80 HKD and up 9.28% over 20 sessions, remains the quality anchor.
New / Most Important

The single most important change is the escalation from verbal support to balance-sheet support for developers, combined with explicit stabilisation guidance to large shareholders [[n0236]]. Together they cap downside in onshore equities without fixing demand, because profit growth is still decelerating [[n0224]]. The Economist's question of how to save China's economy [[n0212]] stays open; the test for investors is whether support reaches household balance sheets rather than only lenders and listed companies.
Playbook ✓

Stay Mixed: own China through quality platforms such as Tencent rather than broad beta, and keep metals exposure light until property credit actually flows. Trigger to add: a confirmed unsecured-loan programme for builders [[n0208]] together with a Shanghai Composite close above 3,031.70 and a positive five-session change. What changes the call: another month of export contraction and consumer-price deflation, which would show policy chasing a weakening economy. ⚠ Divergence: administrative support, from the no-selling guidance to a firmer yuan [[n0187]], is lifting the floor, while profits growth and consumer prices keep sliding [[n0161]]; markets are pricing policy while the economy is still pricing deflation.

geo.label: BOJ ultra-loose under an inflation comeback
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the one major market where inflation is a tailwind for equities rather than a threat. Reuters reports Japan's inflation comeback is prompting investors to tear up old playbooks [[n1103]], and Oxford Economics expects 2024 wage rises to be as high as this year's [[n1145]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 33,447.67, up 9.30% over 20 sessions but down 0.41% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), which reads as consolidation rather than reversal. Fiscal policy leans the same way: Tokyo compiled a $113 billion package to cushion inflation [[n1094]], while September minutes showed Bank of Japan members saw no need for new yield-control tweaks [[n1095]].
Activity & Currency

The currency is the swing factor. LeapRate reports the dollar-yen pair traded sideways despite upbeat Japanese inflation data [[n1135]], and MarketWatch describes the previously invincible US dollar sliding against the yen and the yuan [[n1106]]. A firmer yen shows up in exporter performance: Toyota fell 4.24% over five sessions to 2,770 JPY, while chip-equipment maker Tokyo Electron is up 23.81% over 20 sessions and Advantest 13.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). JAPAN Forward notes Japan losing its rank as the world's third-largest economy [[n1140]], a dollar-terms artefact of a weak currency that reverses if the yen keeps firming.
Playbook ✓

Bullish with a domestic tilt: prefer chip equipment and beneficiaries of wage-driven demand over yen-sensitive exporters such as Toyota. TSMC weighing a next-generation chip fab in Japan [[n0464]] reinforces the semiconductor-capex leg. Trigger to add: a Nikkei 225 close back above 33,447.67 with the five-session change turning positive. What changes the call: a fast yen appreciation that forces exporter guidance cuts, or a yield-control adjustment that lifts JGB yields abruptly and drains the domestic reflation trade.

geo.label: RBA hawkish after hike to 4.35%
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is the developed market where the central bank is still tightening into a slowing consumer. The Reserve Bank lifted rates to a 12-year high of 4.35% [[n0019]], and Governor Bullock now warns that inflation is 'homegrown' [[n0059]]. The ASX 200 closed at 6,987.60, down 1.00% over five sessions and 0.76% in the last (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), lagging the global rally. We stay Bearish until domestic services inflation turns.
Demand & Financing

Demand is splitting. Australian shoppers were tipped to spend more than $6bn over the four-day Black Friday period [[n0075]], but CommBank data show consumers cutting discretionary spending while leaving room for travel and entertainment [[n0041]]. The RBA's own reasoning points at services: hairdressers, dentists and dining out were the price rises that told it to raise rates again [[n0053]]. Institutions are changing too, as Treasurer Jim Chalmers appointed the Bank of England's Andrew Hauser as deputy governor [[n0092]] and plans to axe his own power to override RBA rate calls [[n0086]]. Commonwealth Bank fell 1.04% in the last session to 102.61 AUD.
Playbook ✓

Underweight Australian banks and discretionary retail against the miners; mortgage stress plus sticky services inflation leaves little room for multiple expansion. Trigger to cover: a services-inflation print that lets the RBA signal a peak. What changes the call: Chinese property support moving from down-payment cuts [[n0214]] to developer credit, which would favour BHP and Fortescue, the latter down 3.12% over five sessions, over domestic cyclicals.

geo.label: NBP on hold; handover to a Tusk coalition
parts: Macro Stance

Poland combines the strongest cyclical momentum in Europe with the loudest political noise. Bankier reports real wages rising at their fastest pace in years with nominal pay at a record [[n1222]], Super Biznes reports the first increase in consumption in nine months [[n1256]], and Bankier says Polish industry has finally moved back into positive territory [[n1219]]. Ipsos finds consumer confidence back near pre-pandemic levels [[n1165]], after the economy avoided a technical recession [[n1190]]. The blemish is inflation: GUS revised October CPI slightly higher than first estimated [[n1193]], which makes Governor Glapiński's declaration that Poland no longer has high inflation [[n1184]] look premature. We are Bullish on Polish assets, selectively.
Markets

The market priced the political change early. The USD-listed EPOL ETF closed at 21.77 USD, up 12.80% over 20 sessions, while the PLN-denominated Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker closed at 40.02 PLN, up 5.01% over 20 sessions but down 1.84% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The gap between the two is the currency: Business Insider Polska writes that the zloty is shining globally and forecasts give it more room [[n1271]], and Money.pl frames the strong zloty as a chance for gains on cheaper purchases abroad [[n1263]]. Not everyone is convinced, as Bankier's currency forecast says analysts have not bought into an 'era of a strong zloty' [[n1442]]. Domestically, banks led the latest pullback, with PKO BP down 4.19% and mBank 4.30% over five sessions, while utilities PGE and Tauron jumped 13.19% and 10.15%.
Fiscal & Politics

Monday's swearing-in of Mateusz Morawiecki's new cabinet was a constitutional formality. Notes From Poland calls it a likely temporary government [[n1168]], OKO.press says it was sworn in for two weeks and will fall after 14 days [[n1448]], and Gazeta Prawna writes it has no chance of a confidence vote and no budget [[n1431]]. Morawiecki himself concedes that Poles decided his party needs a coalition partner [[n1424]]. Gazeta Prawna also reports the 2024 budget will be submitted by Donald Tusk's government [[n1320]], and Rzeczpospolita says Tusk's cabinet is assembled with one ministry left to fill [[n1306]]. The fiscal upside is EU money: OKO.press reports €5 billion from the recovery plan will flow despite unmet milestones [[n1225]], and Money.pl reports record budget inflows with Orlen at the top of the list [[n1389]]. The risk is Tusk's flagship pay promise [[n1324]] layered onto a budget written in a hurry.
Corporate & Sectors

Governance of state companies is the equity story. PGE's nuclear venture with ZE PAK received a decision-in-principle for a KHNP plant in Wielkopolska [[n1436]], and Business Insider Polska reports a Ziobro-linked executive leaving PGE's top team [[n1331]]; PGE rose 13.19% over five sessions to 8.15 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The coal miner JSW fell 19.06% over five sessions to 41.20 PLN as Katowice Wyborcza reports a stalled probe into money siphoned from the company [[n1334]]. Orlen chartered a supertanker to buy Venezuelan crude [[n1267]] and, per Wyborcza.biz, will not take over Azoty Puławy [[n1216]]. In consumer names, the billionaire founder is gradually stepping back from LPP [[n1261]], up 16.63% over 20 sessions, while Dino warned a large transaction may not close [[n1253]]. For banks, a Supreme Court ruling that a loan agreement is void because it relied on the bank's own FX tables [[n1367]] keeps the foreign-currency mortgage overhang alive for lenders such as mBank.
Geopolitics & Security

Security spending is structural. Rzeczpospolita reports Poland is building a 54 billion zł air shield that will protect, among other assets, its Patriot batteries [[n1438]]. Counter-intelligence remains busy after Poland charged 16 people over a dismantled Russian spy ring [[n1152]], which BBC Monitoring says sought to disrupt arms supplies to Ukraine [[n1154]]. The near-term economic friction sits at the border: Reuters reports Polish truckers started a round-the-clock blockade of a fourth Ukrainian border crossing [[n1169]], and Al Jazeera shows lorries lining up as the blockade expands [[n1167]]. Defence capex supports domestic industrials and the spending floor of the budget, while the blockade is a transport and Ukraine-relations problem the incoming government inherits.
New / Most Important

The central bank has become a political story. Rzeczpospolita reports the NBP pays millions to Governor Glapiński's advisers and will not disclose their names [[n1429]], Super Biznes reports another PiS politician, a former Morawiecki minister, joining the bank [[n1423]], and Business Insider Polska reports PZU chief executive Beata Kozłowska-Chyła is set to move to the NBP [[n1316]]. Money.pl carries the argument that NBP bond purchases leave 'no room for charges of unconstitutionality' [[n1322]], a defensive framing that shows the programme is contested. Institutional risk at the NBP is the one channel that could reverse the zloty's strength.
Playbook ✓

Overweight Poland through EPOL and domestic consumers such as LPP and Dino, plus utilities with policy tailwinds; stay underweight banks until the foreign-currency mortgage rulings stop multiplying. Trigger to add: the WIG20TR tracker recovering its five-session loss from 40.02 PLN once a Tusk government wins its confidence vote. What changes the call: an open clash between the new government and the NBP that weakens the zloty, the risk Bankier's sceptics already flag [[n1442]]. ⚠ Divergence: the economy is accelerating, with record real wages [[n1222]] and rising consumption [[n1256]], yet the banks that should monetise it are falling, with PKO BP down 4.19% over five sessions, and the central bank's credibility is under fire [[n1429]].
Narrative

AI spending is the earnings engine and the market keeps paying for it: XLK closed at 184.40 USD, up 14.45% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft at 378.61 USD, up 14.80% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The OpenAI governance crisis ended with Sam Altman back as CEO [[n1534]], removing a tail risk to Microsoft's AI roadmap.
Reported

Nvidia's revenue tripled as the AI chip boom continued [[n0331]], and diginomica notes revenue up 200% year-on-year with sovereign AI clouds flagged as the next big opportunity [[n0874]]. That is demand from governments as well as hyperscalers, which lengthens the capex cycle.
EPS Upside Watch

Amazon will offer Salesforce apps on AWS to ease AI integration [[n0658]], a distribution channel that can lift Salesforce's AI attach rates; CRM is up 14.36% over 20 sessions. Adobe, up 21.87% over 20 sessions, shows the market already rewards software with credible AI monetisation.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats AI as a hardware trade. Broadcom closing its $69 billion VMware deal after China's approval [[n0395]] says software consolidation is the next leg, yet AVGO fell 2.92% in the last session: the market is charging for integration risk, and that discount is the opportunity if VMware margins arrive early.
Narrative

Communication services is split between ad-funded platforms facing brand and regulatory risk and subscription models gaining pricing power. XLC closed at 70.52 USD, up 11.78% over 20 sessions, but fell 0.62% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

The New York Times reports X may lose up to $75 million in revenue as more advertisers pull out [[n0917]], budget that is likely to migrate to larger platforms. Telecompaper reports SVOD providers reduced media spend in 2023 [[n1628]], a sign streamers are prioritising margins over subscriber chases.
EPS Upside Watch

Netflix at 479.17 USD, up 20.43% over 20 sessions, is pricing ad-tier and paid-sharing gains; Spotify's plan to grow its share of the multi-billion-dollar music merchandise business [[n0310]] is a margin lever beyond subscriptions, and SPOT is up 14.87% over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The bigger risk to Meta, at 334.70 USD after a 1.04% drop in the last session, is legal rather than cyclical: states claim Meta deliberately targeted young users with addictive technology [[n0932]]. Remedies aimed at youth engagement would hit time spent, the input that sets ad pricing.
Narrative

Financials rallied with the bond market, with XLF at 35.26 USD and up 12.11% over 20 sessions, but a bull-flattening, still-inverted curve is not a net-interest-margin tailwind. KRE is up 13.51% over 20 sessions yet down 2.41% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

CNBC carries KBW's list of the regional banks at greatest risk of being taken over by rivals [[n1633]], consolidation as the answer to deposit costs. Citi is reshuffling bosses in a difficult management overhaul [[n0278]] while losing municipal bankers to Jefferies [[n0672]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits in fees rather than spread. JPMorgan, at 153.19 USD, is expanding payments and corporate banking in Abu Dhabi [[n0706]], and Wells Fargo is gaining market share in Yankee bonds [[n1791]]; capital-markets revenue recovers first when yields fall.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus 'rates down, banks up' trade ignores credit. Economists cited by Business Insider say a default cycle has started amid the Fed's high rates [[n1050]]. If provisions rise while the curve stays inverted, the KRE rally is a short-cover rather than a re-rating, and Goldman Sachs, down 0.44% over five sessions, is the safer way to own a capital-markets rebound.
Narrative

Energy has become the market's funding short. XLE closed at 84.63 USD, flat over 20 sessions while the S&P 500 gained 10.52%, as WTI fell 12.49% to 74.86 USD/bbl and Brent 8.54% to 79.98 USD/bbl over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

CNN reports oil dropped 4% on the OPEC meeting delay [[n1541]], and Business Insider says US gasoline prices have tumbled for two months in their longest streak of declines in over a year [[n1635]]. Venezuela says it is producing 850,000 bpd and hopes to recover US market share [[n0884]].
EPS Upside Watch

At these prices upstream revisions stay negative: Exxon is down 1.51% over 20 sessions and ConocoPhillips 2.55%, leaning on buybacks rather than volume. Henry Hub gas fell 16.65% over 20 sessions to 2.79 USD/MMBtu, removing the winter cushion for gas-weighted producers.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian case is supply discipline, not demand. OPEC's head accused the IEA of vilifying the fossil-fuel industry [[n1626]], the tone of producers ready to defend price. A credible cut at the delayed meeting would catch the sector after a 20-session flatline, and refiners would lag producers because cheaper gasoline already compresses margins.
Narrative

Industrials are split between an aerospace recovery and an agricultural down-cycle. XLI closed at 105.74 USD, up 9.64% over 20 sessions; Boeing is up 22.04% over 20 sessions to 219.30 USD while Deere lost 5.71% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Deere shares tumbled after its 2024 guidance missed estimates [[n0403]], and Agriculture Dive says the company is bracing for a sharp drop in tractor demand despite a profitable year [[n0678]]. L3Harris agreed to sell its commercial aviation business for $800 million [[n0710]], sharpening its defence focus.
EPS Upside Watch

The FAA cleared Boeing flight tests for 737 MAX 10 certification [[n0474]], and Bloomberg reports Airbus and Boeing poised for a major Thai Airways widebody order [[n1581]]. Certification plus widebody demand is the combination that lifts Boeing's free-cash-flow path; Airbus is up 5.86% over 20 sessions to 133.60 EUR.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Logistics models still treat parcel volume as cyclical. WSJ reports Amazon is now the biggest delivery business in the US, ahead of UPS and FedEx [[n0736]], a structural share shift that a cyclical recovery will not reverse.
Narrative
Discretionary is a tale of online winners and store-based losers. XLY closed at 168.51 USD, up 12.65% over 20 sessions, with Amazon at 147.73 USD, up 15.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Lowe's missed sales estimates and cut its outlook [[n0838]], and Nordstrom's sales miss signalled challenges ahead of the holidays [[n0849]]. Against that, Abercrombie & Fitch raised its outlook after a 20% quarterly sales surge [[n0257]], proof that brand heat still beats category weakness.
EPS Upside Watch

WSJ reports Black Friday spending was strong but that how people pay for gifts is upending retailers [[n1743]]; Affirm jumped 11.97% in the last session and 73.48% over 20 sessions as buy-now-pay-later volumes become the swing factor. Barron's frames the Cybertruck's arrival as a hoped-for halo effect for Tesla [[n0738]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Discounting is the hidden cost. Reuters reports US retailers braced for a tough holiday season despite discounts [[n0361]], so record volume bought at markdown is margin-negative. Favour Amazon and off-price over department stores, and treat Home Depot's 12.46% 20-session gain as rate relief rather than demand.
Narrative

Staples lag as investors reprice volume risk. XLP closed at 70.21 USD, up 5.45% over 20 sessions against 10.52% for the S&P 500, and Walmart is down 2.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Morningstar says Walmart's top line expanded as consumers seek value amid tighter economic conditions [[n0819]], and Grocery Dive reports Walmart widening the gap with Amazon in grocery e-commerce [[n0478]]. Share gains at the value end come at the expense of branded suppliers' pricing.
EPS Upside Watch

Morgan Stanley names the stocks most at risk as Ozempic patients eat less [[n0536]], and PepsiCo killing a popular soda [[n0936]] shows portfolio pruning to defend margins. Costco, at 594.90 USD and up 9.55% over 20 sessions, remains the volume winner.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Jim Cramer calls analysts insane to be wary of revolutionary weight-loss drugs [[n0753]]. For staples, the danger is not adoption this year but the multiple that compresses once volume growth looks structurally negative, so Coca-Cola, up 2.10% over five sessions, is a rally to fund from rather than chase.
Narrative

Health care runs at two speeds: GLP-1 leaders against everyone else. XLV closed at 130.31 USD, up 5.82% over 20 sessions, while Eli Lilly at 591.53 USD fell 1.59% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Reuters reports a data analysis finding Lilly's Mounjaro led to more and faster weight loss than Novo's obesity drug [[n1623]]. Novo is investing $2.3 billion in France to boost obesity-drug production [[n0578]], and Lilly plans a new $2.5 billion plant [[n1515]].
EPS Upside Watch

Bloomberg says Lilly's Zepbound is set to be another hit amid the weight-loss frenzy [[n1624]]. Capacity rather than demand sets the earnings path, which is why Novo will cut Victoza production to boost Ozempic supply [[n1550]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Drug-pricing politics is the overlooked risk. Senator Sanders is publicly pressuring Merck, J&J and Bristol Myers Squibb to testify on pricing [[n0343]], and Merck, at 101.43 USD, is down 1.35% over 20 sessions. Pressure on legacy pharma pushes capital into obesity leaders and makes the sector's dispersion wider still.
Narrative

Materials are torn between China hope and European industrial pain. XLB closed at 81.02 USD, up 8.10% over 20 sessions, with Alcoa up 11.87% and Freeport-McMoRan 8.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Copper reached a two-month peak on China demand hopes [[n0175]] before slipping 1.31% over five sessions to 3.76 USD/lb. Fortescue approved a $750 million investment in three green projects [[n0263]], a bet that green iron earns a premium as Chinese steel demand plateaus.
EPS Upside Watch

Gold miners carry the cleanest upside: GDX rose 4.78% over five sessions and Newmont 5.03%, with gold at 2,012.40 USD/oz and silver up 3.62% over five sessions. The Northern Miner expects gold and silver to rise as political and economic risks grind on [[n0129]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Europe is the overlooked risk. The steel sector warns that Germany's budget hole puts industry at risk [[n0510]]; if Berlin's spending freeze persists, European steel and chemicals demand weakens just as China support might lift metals. Favour US-listed miners over European processors.
Narrative

Real estate is the purest equity expression of falling long yields. XLRE closed at 36.45 USD, up 12.67% over 20 sessions and 1.33% over five, as the 10Y fell 45 bps over 20 observations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27) (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Data centres are the growth pocket: TA Realty leased 430 MW across its entire Leesburg data center campus in Virginia [[n1631]]. Housing transactions remain frozen, with US home sales on pace for the worst year since 1993 [[n1714]].
EPS Upside Watch

Lower long yields ease cap-rate pressure and, if mortgage rates follow, unlock residential turnover. Activist Land & Buildings raised its stake in single-family REIT Tricon, calling it substantially undervalued [[n0386]], a signal that private-market buyers see value where public pricing is still stressed.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The St. Louis Fed's analysis of where commercial real-estate financial risks sit [[n1768]] is a reminder that office credit losses are still being recognised. Own data-centre and residential exposure rather than the broad index, because office refinancing does not benefit from a bull flattener.
Narrative

Utilities are both a bond proxy and an AI-power play. XLU closed at 62.79 USD, up 6.91% over 20 sessions, while Constellation Energy is up 12.93% and Vistra gained 2.24% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

MIT Technology Review describes four ways AI is making the power grid faster and more resilient [[n1540]], and Utility Dive asks whether ERCOT can show the way to faster and cheaper grid interconnection [[n1614]]. The EIA says EVs and hybrids reached a record-high 18% of US light-duty vehicle sales [[n1617]], incremental load that supports rate-base growth.
EPS Upside Watch

Nuclear is re-rating: Yahoo Finance's list of the best nuclear energy stocks to buy [[n0648]] reflects the attention, and Cameco is up 19.77% over 20 sessions. Southern, at 70.26 USD and up 5.61% over 20 sessions, offers the regulated version of the same story.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Execution is the overlooked risk. NuScale was hit with an investor lawsuit [[n0450]] and trades at 2.79 USD, down 12.81% over 20 sessions; small modular reactors are not yet investable utility earnings, so own generators with operating nuclear fleets instead.
Narrative

European autos are squeezed between Chinese EV competition and German costs. The STOXX Europe autos tracker closed at 54.31 EUR, down 1.04% over five sessions, and Volkswagen preference shares at 106.12 EUR fell 2.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

CNN reports Volkswagen saying its core VW brand is no longer competitive [[n0746]], while Reuters reports the group struggling with South African costs as it targets savings [[n0590]]. ACEA says European registrations rose 14.6% in October with battery-electric share at 14.2% [[n1518]].
EPS Upside Watch

Stellantis and CATL plan a European factory to make cheaper EV batteries [[n0351]], cost-down that could protect margins, and Stellantis's US line is up 13.19% over 20 sessions. Nissan pledged £2 billion to expand its UK EV hub [[n1586]], adding competition in the mass segment.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Volkswagen's answer is a China-specific entry-level electric platform [[n0592]], a concession that Western platforms cannot compete on cost in China. That is a structural margin reset rather than a cycle, and BMW's 2.41% five-session decline shows premium brands are not immune.
Narrative

Semiconductors remain the AI capex conduit across the US and Asia. SOXX closed at 514.72 USD, up 15.84% over 20 sessions, while Tokyo Electron is up 23.81% and SK Hynix 9.74% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Reported

Tom's Hardware reports Nvidia beat TSMC and Intel to take the chip industry's revenue crown for the first time [[n0908]], and TechPowerUp notes Nvidia earned five times more revenue from AI chips than from gaming GPUs [[n0847]].
EPS Upside Watch

Yahoo Finance expects Marvell to beat earnings estimates [[n0123]], with MRVL at 55.90 USD and up 18.28% over 20 sessions, and Seeking Alpha calls KLA a top pick in the semiconductor industry [[n0708]], with KLAC up 21.62% over 20 sessions. Equipment and networking carry the cleanest operating leverage.
⚡ Breaking Convention

China is the leakage. Dell is prohibiting sales of AMD Radeon and upcoming MI300 GPUs in China [[n0865]], and the TSMC ADR fell 2.38% over five sessions. Export controls shift growth from China-exposed chip designers toward equipment makers serving non-China fabs, which is why Lam Research's 3.16% five-session gain outpaces the designers.

earnings_pattern.title: Margins and guidance beat revenue: the late-November results test
parts: Rewarded

The market paid for margin surprises and raised guidance, not for revenue alone. Abercrombie & Fitch raised its outlook after quarterly sales surged 20% [[n0257]]; Target shares jumped more than 17% after a big earnings beat even as sales fell again [[n0812]]; and Gap surged more than 30% on a sales and earnings beat despite a muted holiday forecast [[n0817]]. Baidu's US line gained 14.71% over five sessions after its third-quarter call [[n0391]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Punished

Weak outlooks were punished regardless of the quarter. Deere tumbled after its 2024 guidance missed estimates [[n0403]] and is down 5.71% over five sessions; Lowe's missed sales estimates and cut its outlook [[n0838]]; Kingfisher issued a second profit warning in two months [[n0872]]; and HP forecast a downbeat first-quarter profit amid a slow PC recovery [[n0835]]. Even Nvidia, which reported record revenue and earnings [[n0848]], is down 2.14% over five sessions.
Pattern

Two rules hold. First, cost discipline beats top line: Target and Gap rallied on margins with sales flat or falling. Second, anything tied to a durable-goods or capex downturn, whether tractors, home improvement or PCs, is sold on the outlook. Bloomberg framed Nvidia's test before the print as whether great is good enough [[n0829]], and in the short run the answer was no; positioning, not fundamentals, set the reaction.
Attention into EPS

Weight-loss drugs were all the rage on third-quarter earnings calls, Reuters reports [[n0823]], and management teams now have to quantify GLP-1 exposure in guidance. The second attention theme is off-price retail: Barron's notes Burlington surging as off-price retailers keep winning [[n0273]]. Both themes reward companies that convert attention into unit growth rather than price.
Playbook

Buy post-earnings drawdowns only where guidance was held and margins expanded; avoid durable-goods names until order guidance stabilises. The next test is Marvell, which Yahoo Finance expects to beat estimates [[n0123]]: a miss on AI networking would extend the beat-and-fade pattern into semiconductors, while a clean raise would confirm that AI suppliers outside Nvidia can still be rewarded.

underowned.title: Uranium and the nuclear fuel chain
parts: Attention Gap

Uranium has rallied while AI absorbed the attention: URA closed at 29.03 USD, up 14.83% over 20 sessions, and Cameco at 45.43 USD is up 19.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The Australian says uranium is on a roll and that this time it looks real [[n1600]].
Exposure & Risk

Reuters reports NZ Funds says its uranium bet returned over 300% [[n1568]], so early holders are sitting on large gains. Exposure runs through Cameco and URA; enrichment via Centrus, down 2.19% over five sessions, carries more policy risk.
Trigger to Watch
A new utility contracting round would confirm demand; a URA close that erases its five-session gain of 1.33% would signal the move is tiring.

underowned.title: The Korea discount
parts: Attention Gap

CNBC asks whether the Korea discount makes the market a value stock or a value trap [[n0734]]. The KOSPI closed at 2,495.66, up 8.01% over 20 sessions, and SK Hynix at 130,700 KRW is up 9.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Exposure & Risk

Samsung Electronics launched a future business division while keeping its two-CEO system [[n0724]], continuity rather than governance reform. Small investors are joining the dispute over a politically motivated ban on short selling [[n1485]], a liquidity distortion that can reverse when the ban lapses.
Trigger to Watch

Samsung, at 71,300 KRW and down 1.93% over five sessions, regaining momentum alongside memory pricing would validate the discount closing; a policy U-turn on shorting would test how much of the rally was mechanical.

underowned.title: Medical devices after the GLP-1 scare
parts: Attention Gap

Moomoo argues the medical-device selloff caused by Ozempic fears has gone too far and that the stocks are rebounding [[n0321]]. Yahoo Finance flags Intuitive Surgical as a trending stock [[n0703]]; ISRG closed at 314.98 USD, up 21.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Exposure & Risk

Medtronic reported second-quarter fiscal 2024 results [[n0842]], keeping large-cap devices in focus. The risk is that real-world data showing Mounjaro more effective than Ozempic [[n0718]] revives the fewer-procedures narrative.
Trigger to Watch
Procedure-volume commentary in the next company updates; ISRG holding its 3.18% five-session gain would show buyers absorbing GLP-1 headlines.

underowned.title: Gold miners versus bullion
parts: Attention Gap

Gold has gone nowhere, at 2,012.40 USD/oz and up only 0.34% over 20 sessions, yet GDX gained 4.78% over five sessions and Newmont 5.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). CBS asks whether gold prices will rise in 2024 [[n1504]].
Exposure & Risk

Miners amplify bullion both ways: Reuters reported gold dropping below $2,000 as the dollar gained and yields pared losses [[n1720]]. Jurisdiction risk is rising, with Mali signing a deal with Russia to build a gold refinery [[n0434]].
Trigger to Watch
DXY breaking below 103.20 with falling real yields; Money.pl reports the NBP enlarging its gold reserves [[n1235]], evidence of official-sector demand.

crypto.title: Bitcoin consolidates as ETF anticipation meets the Binance clean-up
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 37,254.17 USD, down 0.60% on the day and 0.48% over five days but up 5.11% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2023-11-27). Ether closed at 2,027.42 USD after a 1.74% drop, and Solana gave back 4.47% to 55.06 USD after a 27.78% 20-day surge. Forbes notes bitcoin is up 120% this year [[n0768]], and Reuters had it rising 5.7% to $37,802 [[n0769]] as the market shrugged off the Binance case.
New / Most Important

Market structure is improving even as the largest exchange is penalised. Fortune reports Binance's BNB token dropped on criminal charges while bitcoin dipped only slightly [[n0761]]; ex-CEO Changpeng Zhao was released on a $175M bond [[n0767]], and Richard Teng has taken charge as chief executive [[n0794]]. The more important signal is GBTC's discount to NAV falling below 10% for the first time in two years [[n0779]], arbitrage capital betting on conversion to a spot ETF. Coinbase rose to its highest since May 2022 [[n0559]], and COIN is up 69.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Playbook

Hold core bitcoin, but do not lever the ETF story through proxies that already discount it: COIN gained 20.92% and Marathon 12.80% over five sessions. Trigger to add: bitcoin reclaiming the $37,802 level Reuters reported [[n0769]] on a daily close. What changes the call: tighter retail rules spreading, as Singapore's MAS will bar retail customers from buying crypto with local credit cards [[n1484]], or froth signals such as a digital image of a pet rock selling for $268,000 [[n0788]].

flows.title: Liquidity loosens as the dollar heads for its worst month of 2023
parts: Global Liquidity

Financial conditions eased sharply over the month. DXY closed at 103.20, down 3.15% over 20 sessions, and the dollar-denominated EM bond ETF EMB is up 5.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The Financial Times says emerging-market central banks may be trumping the Fed and ECB [[n0981]], with EM easing cycles running ahead of developed ones, and Schroders calls emerging Europe the standout EM region in 2023 [[n0985]]. The counterweight is supply: $7.6 trillion of US government debt matures in the next year [[n0135]], and Bloomberg reports global central bankers warning of uncertainty amid the rate debate [[n0151]]. Easier conditions are being financed by a heavy refinancing calendar, which is why term premium is the variable to watch.
Rates & Dollar

The rates leg is a bull flattener, with the 10Y at 4.39% and the 2Y at 4.84% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). TLT jumped 1.67% in the last session and 8.21% over 20 sessions, while SHY rose only 0.37% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Reuters says the dollar is weakening as the Fed rate-cut view weighs [[n0098]], and BofA Global Research calls 2024 the year of the landing [[n0665]]. ETF.com suggests looking beyond TLT to short-term Treasury ETFs [[n1034]], a hint that the long-duration trade is getting crowded. Gold, at 2,012.40 USD/oz, has barely responded to the softer dollar, a sign that real-rate relief is being expressed in equities and bonds rather than in hard assets.
Credit Check

Spreads have tightened alongside rates: HYG is up 3.80% over 20 sessions and LQD 5.98%. Beneath the surface the cycle is turning. Economists cited by Business Insider say a default cycle has started amid the Fed's high rates [[n1050]], and the ECB warns eurozone banks are showing stress as loan defaults rise [[n0986]]. Liberty Street Economics' work on the nonbank shadow of banks [[n1049]] shows where leverage has migrated, and China's shadow-bank shortfall [[n0209]] is the emerging-market version of the same problem. Tight spreads plus rising defaults is a late-cycle combination that favours investment grade over high yield.
Equity & Fund Flows

Cash is still on the sidelines. Wolf Street reports money market funds, large CDs and small CDs all surged [[n1042]], and Business Insider argues a FOMO rally could hit stocks after investors sold [[n1046]]. Bloomberg Intelligence expects ETFs to see an uptick of trillions in assets [[n1041]], and Kiplinger notes many mutual funds are converting to ETFs [[n1044]], structural plumbing that favours passive index demand. Positioning is crowded in places, with Goldman saying hedge-fund bets on US stocks are the most crowded ever [[n0303]]. Short-dated options are booming too: CNBC reports an exchange expanding its short-term options portfolio as zero-day bets boom [[n1502]], and ARKK is up 33.28% over 20 sessions.
Portfolio Implication

Rotate rather than add gross exposure. Own duration through IEF and quality growth, funded by energy and European autos; keep EM bonds via EMB while the dollar softens; and use the cheap VIX at 12.69 to hedge. Trigger to extend risk: money-market cash rotating into equity funds while DXY holds below 103.20. What changes the call: DXY reclaiming its 20-session-ago level of 106.56, or a jump in high-yield defaults that pulls HYG below its prior close of 75.11 USD, either of which would mean the liquidity impulse is reversing.

anticipatory.title: OPEC+ after the delay: a cut the market is not paying for
parts: What Is Priced

WTI at 74.86 USD/bbl is down 12.49% over 20 sessions and Brent 8.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). CNN reports oil dropped 4% on the OPEC meeting delay [[n1541]], and local US coverage notes pump prices dipping as an OPEC decision looms [[n1619]]. The market is pricing disagreement inside the group, not a deeper cut.
Conditional Expression

If the delayed meeting delivers deeper or extended cuts, the cleanest expression is long XLE and ConocoPhillips, down 2.55% over 20 sessions, against airlines and gasoline-sensitive retailers. If it ends in quota disputes, extend the consumer leg and add to duration as the oil-driven inflation-expectations channel cools further.
Risk

Producers sound combative, with OPEC's head accusing the IEA of vilifying the industry [[n1626]], while Venezuela's output push [[n0884]] adds supply. A WTI close back above its 20-session-ago level of 85.54 would mean the market under-priced cohesion; a break below 74.86 would mean the cut disappointed.

anticipatory.title: Fed cuts in 2024: priced before the data confirm them
parts: What Is Priced

Bank of America says rate cuts are coming next year [[n1786]], and the curve agrees: the 2Y at 4.84% sits well below the 3M bill at 5.49% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). VIX at 12.69 shows equity investors treating the landing as soft.
Conditional Expression

If the next payroll and inflation prints extend the cooling seen in October, when unemployment rose to 3.9% [[n1664]], add to 2Y Treasuries and rate-sensitive equities such as XLRE. If services inflation re-accelerates, the 2Y is the most exposed point on the curve because it has priced the most relief.
Risk

The latest Fed minutes show a consensus that rates need to stay high [[n0294]], and a Bloomberg report has global central bankers warning of uncertainty [[n0151]]. A 2Y move back to the 4.99% of 20 observations ago would unwind a month of easing in one step.

anticipatory.title: Spot bitcoin ETF: the discount is already closing
parts: What Is Priced

GBTC's discount to NAV has fallen below 10% for the first time in two years [[n0779]], and a crypto outlet reports BlackRock and the SEC recently met over spot bitcoin ETF approval [[n0770]]. COIN is up 69.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), so equity proxies already discount a favourable outcome.
Conditional Expression

If approval comes, the remaining upside sits in GBTC's residual discount and in bitcoin itself, not in proxies that have run. If a decision is deferred, expect proxies such as Riot, up 12.79% over five sessions, to fall faster than bitcoin.
Risk

Regulatory reach is widening after the Binance case, and exchange attrition continues as Bittrex Global shuts down [[n0762]]. A bitcoin close below its five-day reference would show the ETF bid fading.

anticipatory.title: China developer lending: from weighing to funding
parts: What Is Priced

The Business Times reports Beijing weighing first-ever unsecured loans to builders [[n0208]], yet the Hang Seng at 17,525.06 is up only 0.68% over 20 sessions and FXI 1.36% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Markets are pricing talk, not money.
Conditional Expression

If a programme is confirmed with named banks and sizes, buy Hong Kong-listed China exposure via FXI and copper miners such as Freeport, with BHP as the lower-beta version. If the measure stays at the consideration stage, fade rallies in China beta and keep exposure in quality platforms such as Tencent.
Risk

Profit growth is slowing [[n0224]] and a shadow-bank shortfall shows losses are still being recognised; support can arrive and still be swamped by falling household confidence. A Shanghai Composite close below 3,031.70 alongside a weaker yuan would mean policy is losing the race.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): record quarter meets a China delay
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia reported record revenue and earnings for its fiscal third quarter [[n0848]], yet shares closed down on a report it delayed a China AI chip designed to comply with US export rules [[n0218]]. Thesis: sovereign-AI and hyperscaler demand outweigh the China leakage.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 482.42 USD, up 0.98% in the last session, down 2.14% over five and up 19.12% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: a second China setback or a broader AI multiple reset.
Trade Expression

Accumulate on closes above 482.42 USD; pair against a semiconductor ETF to isolate execution from sector beta. Exit if the five-session loss deepens while SOXX holds, a sign the market is pricing company-specific China risk.

catalysts.title: Volkswagen (VOW3.DE): restructuring a brand that is 'no longer competitive'
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reports Volkswagen will reduce headcount at its core brand, which management calls no longer competitive [[n0747]]. Thesis: savings take years, while the competitive gap with Chinese EV makers is widening now.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The preference shares closed at 106.12 EUR, down 0.82% in the last session and 2.50% over five, though still up 7.04% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: an aggressive cost target that the market rewards early, as it often does with restructurings.
Trade Expression

Underweight against the STOXX autos tracker. Cover on a close back above the 20-session gain trend with evidence of cuts beyond headcount, such as plant capacity; add if the five-session decline extends below 106.12 EUR.

catalysts.title: Deere (DE): guidance miss meets a right-to-repair ruling
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Agriculture Dive says Deere is bracing for a sharp drop in tractor demand despite a profitable year [[n0678]], and Reuters reports a judge ruled Deere must face US farmers' right-to-repair lawsuits [[n0679]], a threat to high-margin parts and service revenue.
Price Hurdle & Risk

DE closed at 362.21 USD, down 2.16% in the last session and 5.71% over five, almost flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: farm income surprises or buybacks cushioning the downturn.
Trade Expression

Stay short or underweight while the stock trades below 362.21 USD and the five-session trend stays negative. Cover if Caterpillar, down 2.24% over five sessions, and Deere stabilise together, which would signal the capex downturn is priced.

catalysts.title: Eli Lilly (LLY): head-to-head data favours Mounjaro
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reports a real-world study finding Mounjaro more effective than Ozempic for weight loss in overweight and obese adults [[n0718]], and Bloomberg expects Zepbound to be another hit [[n1624]]. Thesis: efficacy leadership plus new capacity converts into share gains against Novo.
Price Hurdle & Risk
LLY closed at 591.53 USD, down 1.59% in the last session and up 5.59% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: supply constraints that cap volumes, and pricing pressure from Washington.
Trade Expression
Buy weakness toward the prior close and hold Lilly against Novo Nordisk's US line, which is up 11.09% over 20 sessions. Reassess if Novo's capacity additions close the supply gap faster than Lilly's.

catalysts.title: Marvell (MRVL): AI networking has to beat a raised bar
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Yahoo Finance expects Marvell to beat earnings estimates [[n0123]]. The thesis is that custom AI silicon and optical networking offset weaker enterprise and carrier demand, but the bar has risen with the stock.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MRVL closed at 55.90 USD, down 0.23% in the last session, up 0.58% over five and up 18.28% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: a beat without a raised AI outlook, which the market has been selling.
Trade Expression

Express through options rather than stock: own upside only if guidance lifts AI revenue expectations. A close above 55.90 USD after results with a positive five-session change confirms; a drop below 47.26 USD, the level of 20 sessions ago, would reverse the month's gains.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA): a founder's reversal and a sliding stock
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNN reports Jack Ma backed off plans to sell Alibaba shares after the stock plunged [[n0517]], and is betting on a new food business in China [[n0241]]. Thesis: the founder's attention is drifting while the restructuring loses momentum.
Price Hurdle & Risk
BABA closed at 77.53 USD, down 1.22% in the last session and 6.39% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: Beijing's market-support measures lift large caps indiscriminately.
Trade Expression
Underweight Alibaba against Tencent within China internet exposure. Cover if BABA reclaims its 20-session-ago level of 82.82 USD or if a buyback acceleration is announced.
